audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph genealogy from Adam through Edom, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for primeval genealogy, nations, Ishmael and Keturah lines, Esau/Seir, Edomite kings and chiefs, gender visibility, ethnic reception, and anti-Amalek misuse. Rich-layer backfill added familiar comparison, verse notes, selected source terms, tags, cross-references, and machine-readable editorial flags.

verses.restored: Adam, Seth, Enosh,

familiar.text: Adam, Sheth, Enosh,

notes.title: Chronicles begins with Adam
notes.body: The genealogy opens with Adam and compresses long ancestral narratives into names. The list functions as a memory map, not a claim that only named males matter.

verses.restored: Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,

familiar.text: Kenan, Mahalaleel, Jered,

verses.restored: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,

familiar.text: Henoch, Methuselah, Lamech,

verses.restored: Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

familiar.text: Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

verses.restored: Sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

familiar.text: The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.

verses.restored: Sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

familiar.text: And the sons of Gomer; Ashchenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.

verses.restored: Sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim/Dodanim.

familiar.text: And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

notes.title: Rodanim / Dodanim
notes.body: The restored text preserves the name variant rather than silently choosing one spelling. Parallel witnesses and Genesis 10 require later source-critical comparison.

verses.restored: Sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

familiar.text: The sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

verses.restored: Sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. Sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.

familiar.text: And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raamah, and Sabtecha. And the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan.

verses.restored: Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be mighty upon earth.

familiar.text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be mighty upon the earth.

notes.title: Mighty
notes.body: The description of Nimrod as mighty reports status or prowess; it is not automatically moral praise or divine endorsement.

verses.restored: Mizraim fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,

familiar.text: And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,

verses.restored: Pathrusim, Casluhim—from whom Philistines came—and Caphtorim.

familiar.text: And Pathrusim, and Casluhim, (of whom came the Philistines,) and Caphthorim.

notes.title: Philistine ancestry line
notes.body: The compressed ancestry notice parallels Genesis 10 and has textual and historical complexities. Ancient genealogical labels must not be mapped directly onto modern populations.

verses.restored: Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn and Heth,

familiar.text: And Canaan begat Zidon his firstborn, and Heth,

verses.restored: also Jebusite, Amorite, Girgashite,

familiar.text: The Jebusite also, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,

verses.restored: Hivite, Arkite, Sinite,

familiar.text: And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,

verses.restored: Arvadite, Zemarite, and Hamathite.

familiar.text: And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.

verses.restored: Sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech/Mash.

familiar.text: The sons of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram, and Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech.

notes.title: Meshech / Mash
notes.body: The final name varies across parallel textual traditions. The slash preserves the unresolved reading rather than hiding the difference.

verses.restored: Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.

familiar.text: And Arphaxad begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber.

verses.restored: To Eber two sons were born: name of one was Peleg, because in his days earth was divided; name of his brother was Joktan.

familiar.text: And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg; because in his days the earth was divided: and his brother’s name was Joktan.

notes.title: Peleg and divided
notes.body: The verse connects Peleg's name with a division of the earth through Hebrew wordplay. The genealogy does not explain exactly what historical event the phrase refers to.

verses.restored: Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

familiar.text: And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,

verses.restored: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

familiar.text: Hadoram also, and Uzal, and Diklah,

verses.restored: Ebal/Obal, Abimael, Sheba,

familiar.text: And Ebal, and Abimael, and Sheba,

notes.title: Ebal / Obal
notes.body: The restored form keeps the parallel-name variation visible for later witness audit.

verses.restored: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.

familiar.text: And Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.

verses.restored: Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,

familiar.text: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,

verses.restored: Eber, Peleg, Reu,

familiar.text: Eber, Peleg, Reu,

verses.restored: Serug, Nahor, Terah,

familiar.text: Serug, Nahor, Terah,

verses.restored: Abram, that is, Abraham.

familiar.text: Abram; the same is Abraham.

notes.title: Abram / Abraham
notes.body: The genealogy explicitly links the earlier name Abram with Abraham, maintaining continuity across the naming transition.

verses.restored: Sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.

familiar.text: The sons of Abraham; Isaac, and Ishmael.

notes.title: Isaac and Ishmael
notes.body: Both sons are retained in the ancestral archive. The list should not be read as permission to erase or degrade Ishmael's descendants.

verses.restored: These are their generations: firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

familiar.text: These are their generations: The firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,

notes.title: Ishmael's firstborn
notes.body: Nebaioth is identified as Ishmael's firstborn. The genealogy preserves Ishmael's family as part of the larger Abrahamic memory.

verses.restored: Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad/Hadar, Tema,

familiar.text: Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema,

verses.restored: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were sons of Ishmael.

familiar.text: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.

notes.title: Sons of Ishmael
notes.body: The closing formula confirms the Ishmaelite line as a remembered branch of Abraham's family, not an alien or disposable people.

verses.restored: Sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine/wife: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.

familiar.text: Now the sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bare Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan; Sheba, and Dedan.

notes.title: Keturah: concubine / wife
notes.body: Chronicles calls Keturah Abraham's concubine, while Genesis 25:1 calls her a wife and Genesis 25:6 refers to Abraham's concubines. The restored wording keeps that textual relationship visible instead of flattening it.

verses.restored: Sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.

familiar.text: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the sons of Keturah.

notes.title: Keturah's descendants
notes.body: The descendants of Keturah remain part of the Abrahamic archive. Their presence should not be used to build later racial or religious hierarchies.

verses.restored: Abraham fathered Isaac. Sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.

familiar.text: And Abraham begat Isaac. The sons of Isaac; Esau and Israel.

notes.title: Esau and Israel
notes.body: Esau and Israel are named together as Isaac's sons. The genealogy preserves kinship even where later narratives describe conflict.

verses.restored: Sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah.

familiar.text: The sons of Esau; Eliphaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.

verses.restored: Sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi/Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.

familiar.text: The sons of Eliphaz; Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek.

notes.title: Timna and Amalek
notes.body: Timna is included inside the family line, and Amalek appears here as an ancestral name. This verse must never be converted into a label for a living ethnic, religious, or political enemy.

verses.restored: Sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

familiar.text: The sons of Reuel; Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

verses.restored: Sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.

familiar.text: And the sons of Seir; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezar, and Dishan.

verses.restored: Sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; Timna was Lotan's sister.

familiar.text: And the sons of Lotan; Hori, and Homam: and Timna was Lotan’s sister.

notes.title: Timna named as sister
notes.body: The line briefly breaks the dominant father-son pattern to name Timna as Lotan's sister. Her presence matters even though the genealogy gives women far less space overall.

verses.restored: Sons of Shobal: Alian/Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi/Shepho, and Onam. Sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.

familiar.text: The sons of Shobal; Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And the sons of Zibeon; Aiah, and Anah.

notes.title: Name variants
notes.body: Alian/Alvan and Shephi/Shepho preserve differences found across parallel forms instead of silently standardizing them.

verses.restored: Son of Anah: Dishon. Sons of Dishon: Hamran/Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.

familiar.text: The sons of Anah; Dishon. And the sons of Dishon; Amram, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.

notes.title: Hamran / Hemdan
notes.body: The restored form keeps a parallel-name variation visible for later witness audit.

verses.restored: Sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

familiar.text: The sons of Ezer; Bilhan, and Zavan, and Jakan. The sons of Dishan; Uz, and Aran.

verses.restored: These are kings who reigned in land of Edom before a king reigned over children of Israel: Bela son of Beor; name of his city was Dinhabah.

familiar.text: Now these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel; Bela the son of Beor: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

notes.title: Edom had kings before Israel
notes.body: The text explicitly remembers Edomite kings before Israelite monarchy. Political organization outside Israel is part of the biblical memory and should not be erased by Israel-centered readings.

verses.restored: Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And when Bela was dead, Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.

verses.restored: Jobab died, and Husham from land of Temanites reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And when Jobab was dead, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead.

verses.restored: Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who struck Midian in field of Moab, reigned in his place; name of his city was Avith.

familiar.text: And when Husham was dead, Hadad the son of Bedad, which smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.

notes.title: Struck Midian
notes.body: The notice records a military victory as part of royal memory. Description of conquest is not moral authorization for violence against later peoples.

verses.restored: Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And when Hadad was dead, Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.

verses.restored: Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth by river reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And when Samlah was dead, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.

verses.restored: Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And when Shaul was dead, Baalhanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.

verses.restored: Baal-hanan died, and Hadad/Hadar reigned in his place; name of his city was Pai/Pau, and name of his wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.

familiar.text: And when Baalhanan was dead, Hadad reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pai; and his wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

notes.title: Mehetabel, Matred, Me-zahab
notes.body: Three generations of women are named within the royal genealogy. Their naming should not be treated as incidental simply because most of the chapter is patrilineal.

notes.title: Hadad / Hadar; Pai / Pau
notes.body: The restored text keeps variant forms visible rather than choosing a single spelling without a full witness audit.

verses.restored: Hadad died. Chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Aliah/Alvah, chief Jetheth,

familiar.text: Hadad died also. And the dukes of Edom were; duke Timnah, duke Aliah, duke Jetheth,

notes.title: Chiefs, not modern dukes
notes.body: The Hebrew title is better understood as clan chief or leader. The familiar KJV uses duke, an English historical title that can mislead modern readers.

notes.title: Aliah / Alvah
notes.body: The restored text preserves a name variant for later textual comparison.

verses.restored: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

familiar.text: Duke Aholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon,

notes.title: Chiefs, not modern dukes
notes.body: The Hebrew title is better understood as clan chief or leader. The familiar KJV uses duke, an English historical title that can mislead modern readers.

verses.restored: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

familiar.text: Duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar,

notes.title: Chiefs, not modern dukes
notes.body: The Hebrew title is better understood as clan chief or leader. The familiar KJV uses duke, an English historical title that can mislead modern readers.

verses.restored: chief Magdiel and chief Iram. These were chiefs of Edom.

familiar.text: Duke Magdiel, duke Iram. These are the dukes of Edom.

notes.title: Chiefs, not modern dukes

translation_notes: Genealogies are selective social memory, not complete biological records and not rankings of human worth.
Names later associated with nations must not be racialized or used to assign inherited guilt to modern peoples.
Ishmael, Keturah, Esau, Seir, and Edom are preserved within the family archive rather than erased from it.
Edomite kings are explicitly remembered before Israel had a king; Israel is not presented as the only people with history or political organization.
Timna, Mehetabel, Matred, Me-zahab, Keturah, and other named women show that women are present even when patrilineal form often obscures them.
Amalek in verse 36 is an ancestral name within an ancient genealogy and may never be mapped onto any living population.
Textual variants in names—including Rodanim/Dodanim and several Edomite names—require later Hebrew, Greek, and parallel-text audit.
safety_note: Do not use this genealogy to construct racial hierarchies, blood purity, nationalism, antisemitism, anti-Arab hatred, anti-Edomite typologies, or modern Amalek targeting. Every named lineage represents human communities whose descendants cannot inherit ancient blame.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare 1 Chronicles 1 with Genesis 5, 10, 11, 25, and 36 for compressed genealogy and name variants.
Rodanim/Dodanim, Meshech/Mash, Ebal/Obal, Hadad/Hadar, Zephi/Zepho, Alian/Alvan, Shephi/Shepho, Hamran/Hemdan, Pai/Pau, and related forms require manuscript/parallel witness review.
Keturah's designation should be read alongside Genesis 25:1 and 25:6 rather than harmonized silently.
